Six hypotheses committed before fitting (after viewing descriptives; commit a08c5b7), 11 tests on 5,587 repositories (negative binomial / logistic, HC1, Benjamini-Hochberg); 99 exploratory tests on 5,586 sets; adopters vs 4,699 matched non-adopters by star tier and language; paired AGENTS.md vs CLAUDE.md comparison (484 repositories)

N/A for configurations. Adoption 26.3% overall, 23.2% (lowest tier) to 59.6% (89 most-starred); 40.8% TypeScript to 13.0% C. Of 2,388 with both files, CLAUDE.md defers to AGENTS.md in 1,540, reverse 182, separate 598; new adopters shifted to AGENTS.md first. 74.0% of directives give no reason; 10.8% cite an incident; AI attribution in commits prohibited by 7.5% vs required by 59 repos; PR AI disclosure required 5.8% vs prohibited 1.9%. 15.8% match an /init signature (11.5% claude /init); 33.1% carry some origin trace; 81.8% edited after creation. Hypotheses: H3 (compiled languages -> build statements, OR 1.68), H5 (CLAUDE.md more descriptive, +6.3 pp), H6 (stars -> PR/AI-policy rules, OR 1.36) supported; H2 mixed; H1, H4 not supported. LLM/agent projects over-represented among adopters (OR 2.76; 1.54 post hoc)

N/A for configurations. Method caveat: models agree with each other much more than with the human reviewer (subject area 43-50%, kind kappa 0.33-0.40), so topic results are model-defined. Limitations stated: presence/content of root files only, not run-time instructions; AI-marked commits partial; LLM categories diverge from human reading; 60-statement single-coder review stopped early; vendor models analysing their own format; survivorship and renames in history; cross-sectional; one snapshot; stars gameable; many small effects significant

Threats: construct, measurement, internal, external validity (as above). Open questions: whether reasons or emphasis change agent behaviour; whether repositories follow their own instructions (e.g. AI-attribution rules); confirmatory tests of exploratory associations on fresh data
